title: Release slate synchronization and rollout notes automation for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Objective: create a synchronized release slate and an automated release-notes pipeline that stitches changes across API, Console, and Runtime components into a single consumer-facing release narrative and a set of per-team cut criteria. This ticket covers: 1) agreeing on a phased scope-freeze window per component (API / Console / Runtime), 2) implementing a lightweight "release-notes bot" that aggregates merged PR metadata and staged screenshots, and 3) a rollout choreography that ties canary percentages and gating telemetry to release notes publication.

Why this is different: previous artifacts are playbooks and cut matrices; this work focuses on operationalizing the orchestration (automation + explicit telemetry gates) so PMs and GTM get reliable, near-real-time release signals and auto-drafted release notes to reduce manual coordination overhead.

Key deliverables: 
- Phase-based scope-freeze calendar (API: freeze D-7 for schema/stable endpoints; Console: freeze D-5 for UX changes; Runtime: freeze D-10 for kernel/config changes).
- Cut criteria matrix with measurable signals (see below).
- Release-notes automation service (GitHub Actions + small lambda) that collects: PR titles, cherry-picked changelog snippets, signed-off screenshots from design Google Drive, and relevant test-ground-truth perf dashboards. Generates a draft release-notes PR in docs repo.
- Cross-team roll-out choreography doc with canary plan, fallback triggers, and comms template for Support/Success/Marketing.

Cut criteria (high-level, metric thresholds are for gating):
- Block release if P99 token generation latency increases > 20% compared to baseline over 1h rolling window.
- Block release if request error rate (5xx + model-timeout) > 0.5% sustained over 30m across canary nodes.
- Block release if rate of downstream integration failures (webhooks/ingest) increases by > 10% relative to baseline.
- Block release if any infra migration (runtime quantized kernels) triggers degraded KV cache hit-rate drop > 15%.
- All security fixes with severity >= high must be merged and validated before scope-lock.

Rollout plan (recommended default):
1) Canary 1 (5% traffic, 24h): monitor p99/p95, error rate, infra CPU/GPU saturation.
2) Canary 2 (20% traffic, 24h): repeat checks, validate cost-trending dashboard.
3) Ramp to 60% (48h) then full rollout if no gating signals.
4) Auto-rollback policy: immediate rollback on any single canary node 5xx spike > 3x baseline or sustained P95 increase > 30% for 30m.

GTM / Release notes specifics: 
- Release-notes bot will open a docs PR with: high-level bullets, per-component callouts, screenshots, notable API changes and migration notes, and "known issues" block populated from Jira/Linear labels.
- Marketing checklist (in the PR template): hero screenshot, 1-line product highlight, customer quote placeholder, and embargo flag.
- Support checklist (auto-added to PR): playbook link, rollback runbook link, incident contacts.

Trade-offs and open questions: 
- Tight automation reduces manual errors but requires maintenance (who owns bot infra?). Proposal: assign infra ownership to Platform/Engineer on-call for the release window and rotate afterwards.
- Scope-freeze cadence is staggered to reduce last-minute dependency friction; could increase complexity for cross-component features that require simultaneous changes. For those, use a separate coordinated "cross-cut" lane (see action items).

Success metrics (post-release): 
- Release notes PR generated automatically for 90% of releases.
- Reduction in cross-team status sync meetings by 30% during release week.
- Time-to-publish release notes after final merge < 2 hours.
